# d402

> d402 ("data 402") lets an agent pay for API access by labelling data instead of sending money.
> A gated route answers `402 Payment Required` with an offer in the same `accepts` shape as x402.
> The agent labels a small bundle of items (some are hidden control items), signs its answers with an Ed25519 key, gets a voucher worth N calls, and retries with it.

No wallet, no account, no API key. The seller gets a labelled dataset. Protocol version 1. The full spec is inlined in https://napoleon1313.github.io/d402-site/llms-full.txt

## If you are an agent and you just got a 402 with d402 in accepts, do this

Find the entry in `accepts` whose `scheme` is `"d402"`. Read its `hint`: it says the same as this paragraph for that seller. Make an Ed25519 keypair once and keep it (your trust history is tied to the key). `GET {taskUrl}?tier={smallest tier id}` with header `D402-Key: <your public key, base64url, no padding>`. You get a bundle: `bundleId`, `labels`, `items`. Label every item with exactly one of `labels`; you are not told which items are controls, so label all of them honestly. `POST {taskUrl}/{bundleId}` with header `D402-Key` and JSON body `{"answers": {"<itemId>": "<label>", ...}, "sig": "<signature>"}`, where the signature is over `"d402:submit\n" + bundleId + "\n" + canonicalJSON(answers)`. On `200` you get `{voucher, calls, scope, expiresAt}`. Retry the original request with header `D402-Voucher: <voucher>`. Keep the voucher and reuse it for later calls on any path in `scope` until `D402-Calls-Remaining` reaches 0 or a spend answers 402 again. On `422 quality`, get a new bundle and label more carefully.

## The 402 offer

Served on any gated route without a valid voucher, and on `GET /.well-known/d402` (so you can earn before you need it).

```json
{
  "d402": "1",
  "accepts": [
    {
      "scheme": "d402",
      "sellerId": "api.example.com",
      "taskUrl": "https://api.example.com/.well-known/d402/tasks",
      "taskTypes": ["classify"],
      "scope": ["/search"],
      "voucherTtl": 86400,
      "hint": "No wallet needed. To get 10 calls on /search: GET .../tasks?tier=s with a D402-Key header, ...",
      "tiers": [
        { "id": "s", "items": 5,  "est_tokens": 1000,  "reward": { "calls": 10 } },
        { "id": "m", "items": 25, "est_tokens": 5000,  "reward": { "calls": 60 } }
      ]
    }
  ],
  "error": "missing_voucher"
}
```

- `taskUrl`: absolute URL of the task endpoint.
- `scope`: path prefixes the voucher is valid for.
- `tiers[].items`: bundle size; `reward.calls`: calls the voucher is worth; `est_tokens`: advisory cost.
- `hint`: plain-language instructions for this seller. Follow it.
- `error` (only on a 402 from a gated route): `missing_voucher`, `voucher_invalid`, `voucher_expired`, `voucher_exhausted`, `scope_mismatch`, and on sellers that bind vouchers `bad_key`, `stale_timestamp`, `bad_signature`, `replayed_spend`.
- Other schemes may sit beside d402 in `accepts` (x402 `exact`, `mpp`). The d402 entry is first.

## Task endpoints

- `GET {taskUrl}?tier=<id>` with `D402-Key` (and optional `D402-Model: claude|gpt|gemini|llama|...`). Returns `{bundleId, tier, type, instructions, labels, items: [{id, text}], expiresAt}`. Bundles expire after 600 s by default.
- `POST {taskUrl}/{bundleId}` with `D402-Key` and `Content-Type: application/json`, body `{answers, model?, sig}`. Returns `200 {voucher, calls, scope, expiresAt}` or an error.
- Errors are JSON `{"error": code, "message": string}`: `bad_tier` (400), `no_tasks` (409), `rate_limited` (429, honour `Retry-After`), `blocked` (403), `missing_key` / `bad_key` (400), `unknown_bundle` (404), `expired_bundle` (410), `bad_signature` (401), `already_submitted` (409), `incomplete` / `bad_label` (400), `quality` (422: the bundle failed; the seller never says which items were wrong).

## Headers

| Header | Direction | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `D402-Key` | agent to seller | base64url Ed25519 public key (32 raw bytes, no padding). Required on task endpoints. |
| `D402-Voucher` | agent to seller | the voucher JWT. Required on spend. |
| `D402-Model` | agent to seller | optional model family. |
| `D402-Timestamp` | agent to seller | unix seconds. Bound spends only. |
| `D402-Nonce` | agent to seller | 16 random bytes, base64url. Bound spends, recommended. |
| `D402-Sig` | agent to seller | base64url Ed25519 signature. Bound spends only. |
| `D402-Calls-Remaining` | seller to agent | calls left on the voucher, on every successful spend. |

## Signing

Ed25519 over the UTF-8 bytes of these strings; signatures are base64url without padding. `\n` is a newline byte.

```
submit:      "d402:submit\n" + bundleId + "\n" + canonicalJSON(answers)
bound spend: "d402:spend\n" + METHOD + "\n" + path + "\n" + jti + "\n" + timestamp + "\n" + nonce
```

- `canonicalJSON`: JSON with object keys sorted recursively and no whitespace. Python: `json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(",", ":"), ensure_ascii=False)`.
- Bound spends are needed only when the seller sets `bindVouchers`. Send `D402-Key` (must equal the voucher's `sub`), `D402-Timestamp` (within 300 s of the seller's clock), `D402-Nonce` (fresh per request) and `D402-Sig`. `path` is the request path without the query; `jti` is the voucher JWT's `jti` claim. Without a nonce the signed string has 5 lines (no trailing nonce line). Sending these headers to a seller that does not bind vouchers is harmless.

## Vouchers

`D402-Voucher: <jwt>` on any request whose path starts with a `scope` prefix. The JWT (HS256, minted by the seller) has claims `iss`, `sub` (your public key), `scope`, `jti`, `iat`, `exp`. The calls counter lives on the seller under `jti`. One voucher is valid only at the seller that minted it.

<!-- spec/SPEC.md, inlined verbatim at build time from https://github.com/napoleon1313/d402/blob/main/spec/SPEC.md -->

# d402 protocol, version 1

d402 ("data 402") is an HTTP payment scheme where an agent pays for API access by
labelling data instead of sending money. It uses the same `402 Payment Required`
handshake and `accepts` array shape as x402, so a seller can offer USDC and d402
side by side and the agent picks.

The model is reCAPTCHA for agents:

1. Gate. No access without a voucher.
2. The challenge is useful work. The seller gets labelled data.
3. Verification by control items. Every bundle mixes in "golden" items with known
   answers. The agent is never told which. Pass the goldens, get the voucher.
   Answers on unknown items become weighted votes.
4. Trust. Keys with a clean history see fewer goldens and bigger rewards.

## 1. Roles

- Seller: runs an HTTP API, gates routes, owns a task pool, mints vouchers.
- Agent: holds an Ed25519 keypair, earns vouchers by answering bundles, spends them.
- Solver: the code inside the agent that turns a bundle into answers (usually an LLM call).

## 2. Headers

| Header | Direction | Value |
|---|---|---|
| `D402-Key` | agent -> seller | base64url Ed25519 public key (32 raw bytes). Required on task endpoints. Optional on spend. |
| `D402-Voucher` | agent -> seller | the voucher JWT. Required on spend. |
| `D402-Model` | agent -> seller | optional model family string, e.g. `claude`, `gpt`, `gemini`, `llama`. Used for the diversity rule. |
| `D402-Timestamp` | agent -> seller | unix seconds. Required only when the seller binds spend to the key. |
| `D402-Sig` | agent -> seller | base64url Ed25519 signature. Required only when the seller binds spend to the key. |
| `D402-Nonce` | agent -> seller | 16 random bytes, base64url. Recommended on bound spends; see 7.2. |
| `D402-Calls-Remaining` | seller -> agent | integer, on every successful spend. |

## 3. Discovery and the 402 offer

A gated route without a valid voucher returns `402` with this JSON body. The same
body is served on `GET /.well-known/d402` so agents can earn ahead of time.

```json
{
  "d402": "1",
  "accepts": [
    {
      "scheme": "d402",
      "sellerId": "api.example.com",
      "taskUrl": "https://api.example.com/.well-known/d402/tasks",
      "taskTypes": ["classify"],
      "scope": ["/search"],
      "voucherTtl": 86400,
      "hint": "No wallet needed. To get 10 calls on /search: GET .../tasks?tier=s with a D402-Key header, label the 5 items, POST signed answers, retry with the voucher.",
      "tiers": [
        { "id": "s", "items": 5,  "est_tokens": 1000,  "reward": { "calls": 10 } },
        { "id": "m", "items": 25, "est_tokens": 5000,  "reward": { "calls": 60 } },
        { "id": "l", "items": 50, "est_tokens": 10000, "reward": { "calls": 150 } }
      ]
    }
  ]
}
```

- `taskUrl` is absolute.
- `taskTypes` lists the task types (section 8) the seller's pool holds, `classify`
  first. A seller whose pool holds only classify items lists `["classify"]`.
- `hint` (optional) is plain-language text telling an agent that has never seen d402
  what to do: where to get a bundle, how many items, what it earns, how to sign. Sellers
  should include it. Agents find their way through a 402 far more often when the body
  tells them what to do than when it only names a scheme.
- `scope` is a list of path prefixes the voucher is valid for.
- `tiers[].items` is the number of items in a bundle, at least 2 (every bundle holds at
  least one golden and one unknown item). `est_tokens` is advisory,
  so the agent can budget in its own unit. The seller grades in items.
- Other schemes (for example x402's `exact`) may appear in `accepts`.

## 4. Earning a bundle

```
GET {taskUrl}?tier=m[&type=pairwise]
    D402-Key: <pubkey>
    D402-Model: claude            (optional)
```

A bundle holds items of one task type, named by its `type` field. A seller's pool
may hold items of several types. The agent may ask for one with `type`; without it
the seller serves, among the types in `taskTypes`, the one with the most open unknown
items for this key that also has enough live goldens (ties go to the type listed
first).

Response `200`:

```json
{
  "bundleId": "b_01J...",
  "tier": "m",
  "type": "classify",
  "instructions": "Label each item with exactly one of the labels.",
  "labels": ["sports", "business", "tech", "world"],
  "items": [ { "id": "i_1", "text": "..." }, { "id": "i_2", "text": "..." } ],
  "expiresAt": 1760000000
}
```

A pairwise bundle (section 8) has the same envelope:

```json
{
  "bundleId": "b_01K...",
  "tier": "m",
  "type": "pairwise",
  "instructions": "Pick the better answer to the prompt: a or b.",
  "labels": ["a", "b"],
  "items": [ { "id": "p_1", "prompt": "...", "a": "...", "b": "..." } ],
  "expiresAt": 1760000000
}
```

Errors (`4xx`, JSON `{ "error": code, "message": string }`):

- `bad_tier`: unknown tier id.
- `bad_request`: `type` is not a known task type.
- `no_tasks` (status `409`): the pool has nothing to hand out, or no unknown item is left
  for this key; every bundle holds at least one unknown item. Also returned when the
  requested `type` is not in `taskTypes`.
- `rate_limited`: too many bundles for this key or IP. `Retry-After` header is set.
- `blocked`: the key's trust is below the floor (status `403`).
- `missing_key` / `bad_key`: `D402-Key` absent or not a valid key.

Bundles expire. Default 600 seconds. An expired bundle gets `expired_bundle` on submit.

## 5. Submitting answers

```
POST {taskUrl}/{bundleId}
    D402-Key: <pubkey>
    Content-Type: application/json

{
  "answers": { "i_1": "tech", "i_2": "sports" },
  "model": "claude",
  "sig": "<base64url ed25519 signature>"
}
```

`sig` is over the UTF-8 bytes of:

```
"d402:submit\n" + bundleId + "\n" + canonicalJSON(answers)
```

`canonicalJSON` is JSON with object keys sorted recursively and no whitespace.

Response `200` (bundle passed):

```json
{ "voucher": "<jwt>", "calls": 60, "scope": ["/search"], "expiresAt": 1760086400 }
```

Response `422` (bundle failed): `{ "error": "quality", "message": "..." }`.
The seller never reveals which items were golden or which were wrong.

Other errors: `unknown_bundle`, `expired_bundle`, `bad_signature`, `already_submitted`,
`incomplete` (an item has no answer), `bad_label` (answer not in `labels`).

Answers are graded the same way for every task type: each answer must be one of the
bundle's `labels`.

### 5.1 Grading rule (v1)

- Let `g` be the number of golden items in the bundle, `c` the number answered correctly.
- Every bundle contains at least 1 golden item.
- The bundle passes when `c / g >= 0.8`, and when `g == 1` it passes only when `c == 1`.
- On pass: mint a voucher, record every answer on unknown items as a vote with weight
  equal to the agent's current accuracy estimate.
- On fail: no voucher. The bundle's unknown answers are discarded.
- Either way the agent's golden counters are updated.

### 5.2 Trust and golden ratio

Per key, the seller keeps `goldenSeen`, `goldenCorrect`, `bundles`.

- `accuracy = (goldenCorrect + 1) / (goldenSeen + 2)` (Laplace prior).
- Golden ratio for the next bundle:
  - `bundles < 5`: 0.4
  - `bundles >= 50` and `accuracy >= 0.95`: 0.1
  - `bundles >= 10` and `accuracy >= 0.9`: 0.2
  - otherwise 0.4
- Golden count per bundle: `max(1, round(items * ratio))`.
- When fewer unknown items are available to the key than the bundle has room for, the
  seller tops the bundle up with more goldens, but a bundle always keeps at least one
  unknown item: with no unknown left for the key (none open, or all already answered or
  held in an open bundle by this key) the seller answers `no_tasks` instead of handing out
  an all-golden bundle, so goldens alone never earn a voucher.
- A key with `bundles >= 5` and `accuracy < 0.6` is blocked. Task endpoints return
  `403 blocked`. Existing vouchers keep working until they expire.

### 5.3 Resolving unknown items

An unknown item is resolved when, for its top answer:

- the sum of vote weights is `>= 2.0`, and
- at least 2 distinct keys voted for it, and
- if the seller enables `requireModelFamilies`, at least 2 distinct declared model
  families voted for it.

Resolved items leave the pool. The seller can export them.

Note: because `accuracy` uses a Laplace prior it is always below 1.0, so 2 voters
can never reach a weight of 2.0 on their own. In practice an item resolves on its
3rd agreeing vote from distinct keys. This is intended: 3-way agreement is the
redundancy level that makes the resolved label worth more than a single agent's.

### 5.4 Golden rotation

A golden item is retired after `goldenMaxExposures` (default 200) bundles.

## 6. The voucher

An HS256 JWT minted and verified by the seller. Claims:

```json
{ "iss": "api.example.com", "sub": "<agent pubkey>", "scope": ["/search"],
  "jti": "v_01J...", "iat": 1760000000, "exp": 1760086400 }
```

Remaining calls are stored server-side keyed by `jti`. The token is stateless, the
counter is not.

## 7. Spending

```
GET /search?q=...
    D402-Voucher: <jwt>
```

Seller checks: signature, `exp`, path matches a `scope` prefix, `jti` known,
calls remaining `> 0`. Decrements by 1 and serves the route. Response carries
`D402-Calls-Remaining`.

Failures return `402` with the offer body and an extra top-level `"error"` field:
`voucher_invalid`, `voucher_expired`, `voucher_exhausted`, `scope_mismatch`.

### 7.1 Bound spending (optional)

When the seller sets `bindVouchers: true`, spend requests must also carry
`D402-Key`, `D402-Timestamp` and `D402-Sig`, where the signature is over:

```
"d402:spend\n" + method + "\n" + path + "\n" + jti + "\n" + timestamp
```

`path` is the request path without query. `D402-Key` must equal the voucher's `sub`.
Timestamps older than 300 seconds are rejected (`stale_timestamp`). A leaked voucher
is then useless without the private key.

### 7.2 Spend nonce (recommended with bound spending)

Section 7.1 alone lets a captured bound spend be replayed for up to 300 seconds,
burning a call each time. To close that, the agent sends `D402-Nonce` (16 random
bytes, base64url) and appends it as a 6th line of the signed message:

```
"d402:spend\n" + method + "\n" + path + "\n" + jti + "\n" + timestamp + "\n" + nonce
```

The seller verifies with the nonce when the header is present and remembers
`(jti, nonce)` until the timestamp leaves the skew window. A repeated pair is
rejected with `replayed_spend`. Sellers may set `requireSpendNonce` to reject
bound spends that carry no nonce; by default the 5-line form is still accepted
so older clients keep working.

### 7.3 Other schemes in the same 402

A seller may offer other payment schemes beside d402. Each scheme can add entries
to `accepts`, top-level body fields (x402 adds `x402Version`), and response
headers (MPP adds `WWW-Authenticate: Payment ...`). The gate routes a request by
what it carries: a `D402-Voucher` header always takes the d402 path; otherwise
the first scheme whose credential header is present verifies it. A failed
scheme payment returns `402` with `error: "payment_failed"` and a `schemeError`
object `{ scheme, error, message }`. The d402 entry stays first in `accepts`.

## 8. Task types

v1 defines `classify` and `pairwise`. Both use the same bundle envelope, the same
answer shape (one of `labels` per item id), the same goldens and the same grading
and resolution rules (sections 5.1 to 5.4).

`classify`:

- bundle fields: `labels: string[]`, `items: { id, text }[]`
- answer: one of `labels` per item id

`pairwise` (preference between two answers to one prompt):

- bundle fields: `labels: ["a", "b"]`, or `["a", "b", "tie"]` when the seller allows
  ties; `items: { id, prompt, a, b }[]`
- `instructions` default: "Pick the better answer to the prompt: a or b."
- answer: one of `labels` per item id (`a` means answer `a` is better)

Clients that only read `labels` and item ids can stay generic across both types.
An exported resolved pairwise item carries `type: "pairwise"`, `prompt`, `a` and `b`
beside the usual `id`, `answer`, `weight` and `voters` (its `text` is empty); a
resolved classify item keeps its v1 shape `{ id, text, answer, weight, voters }`.

Reserved for later: `extract`, `telemetry`.

## 9. Rate limits (defaults)

- 60 bundles per key per hour
- 120 bundles per IP per hour
- At most 5 open (unsubmitted, unexpired) bundles per key

## 10. Seller task file format

JSONL, one item per line:

```json
{ "id": "i_1", "type": "classify", "text": "...", "golden": "tech" }
{ "id": "i_2", "type": "classify", "text": "..." }
{ "id": "p_1", "type": "pairwise", "prompt": "...", "a": "...", "b": "...", "golden": "a" }
{ "id": "p_2", "type": "pairwise", "prompt": "...", "a": "...", "b": "..." }
```

`golden` present means the item is a control item with that answer. `type` defaults
to `classify` when absent. A pairwise golden is `a`, `b` or `tie`; `tie` only when the
seller allows ties. One file may mix both types.

## 11. Security notes

- Per-item results are never revealed.
- Goldens are sampled uniformly from the live golden pool and retired after N exposures.
- Vouchers are bearer tokens unless `bindVouchers` is on. Sellers that care should turn it on,
  and set `requireSpendNonce` so a captured spend cannot be replayed inside the skew window.
- Key and IP rate limits are the only Sybil defence in v1. A coordinated farm with many
  keys sharing golden answers is out of scope for v1.
